Use the Slurm backend when a shared GPU cluster schedules work with `sbatch`.
`bionemor` reads allocation state with `sacct` and cancels jobs with `scancel`.
It currently submits one-node jobs.

These examples were pre-rendered on 2026-08-01 from package revision
8819b8ec4d86, but were not executed on a Slurm cluster. Treat them as
configuration templates until scheduler, shared filesystem, container runtime,
and allocation behavior have been validated on your cluster.

## Cluster requirements

Before using this backend, confirm that:

- The submitting process can call `sbatch`, `sacct`, and `scancel`.
- The login node, compute nodes, and container see the workspace at the same
  absolute path.
- GPU allocations provide an NVIDIA CUDA GPU.
- Compute nodes provide `bash`, `awk`, `mkfifo`, and the same `Rscript` path
  used to submit the job; that R installation needs `jsonlite`.
- Apptainer is available on compute nodes when `engine = "container"`.
- `sha256sum` is available when using a local SIF image.

Slurm support is experimental. `bionemo_install()` verifies the BioNeMo runtime
inside a synchronous Slurm allocation; it does not require GPU or Apptainer
probes to pass on the login host.

## Use an administrator-managed runtime

Use `engine = "external"` when the pinned BioNeMo Recipes commands and package
helper are already available on compute nodes:


``` r
library(bionemor)

compute <- bionemo_compute(
  backend = "slurm",
  engine = "external",
  workspace = "/shared/projects/evo2",
  gpus = 4L,
  queue = "gpu",
  account = "biology",
  walltime = "01:00:00"
)

compute <- bionemo_install(compute)
bionemo_doctor(compute, target = "training", verbose = FALSE)
```

## Use an existing Apptainer image

Use `engine = "container"` with an existing Apptainer image built from the
verified Evo 2 recipe:


``` r
compute <- bionemo_compute(
  backend = "slurm",
  engine = "container",
  image = "/shared/images/bionemor-evo2-e8e7f597.sif",
  workspace = "/shared/projects/evo2",
  gpus = 4L,
  queue = "gpu"
)

compute <- bionemo_install(compute)
```

For a local SIF path, `bionemo_install()` computes and records its SHA-256
digest before submitting verification probes. The image must be readable on the
shared filesystem. A digest-qualified image URI records the supplied digest.

`bionemor` does not build a SIF on a compute node or select cluster modules.
Prepare the image and required modules before running these examples.

## Submit and reopen a job


``` r
candidate_sequences <- c(
  reference = "ACGTACGTACGT",
  variant = "ACGTACGTTCGT"
)

model <- evo2(
  "7b",
  checkpoint = "/shared/models/evo2-7b-mbridge",
  compute = compute
)

job <- evo2_score(
  model,
  candidate_sequences,
  async = TRUE
)

path <- job_path(job)
job_status(job)
job_logs(job, tail = 100L)

job <- bionemo_job(path)
result <- job_wait(job, timeout = 600)
```

A `job_wait()` timeout does not cancel the allocation. Call `job_cancel()` to
issue `scancel`.
